text:
The probe sent to explore the Marisol Trench reached a depth of 6,100 metres on 14 March 2031, according to the Calder Basin Oceanographic Institute.

The finding is set out in Mission Summary Report CB-31-07, which the institute released the day after the dive. The report states that the probe transmitted its final sounding on reaching maximum depth.

Descent took 4 hours 52 minutes. The probe's pressure sensors logged 610 bar at the lowest point, the report says.

Dr. Ilvane Torsk, the institute's chief scientist, led the mission. The report credits her team with directing the descent and with recovering the final transmission.

The summary gives the depth and pressure readings as the mission's principal results. The institute has not, in the document, described any further stages of the programme.
